env_keys.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
env_keys.display: GitHub personal access token (optional — fallback if you don't sign in)

recipes.description: Generic HTTP fetch tool: the model can request a URL and read the response. No credentials required; the recipe imposes no allow-list — limit access via Cedar policy if you need a domain whitelist.
recipes.warning: Python server (PyPI mcp-server-fetch) launched via uvx; requires uv installed. First run downloads the package (5–15 s).

recipes.description: Web and local search via the Brave Search API. Requires a Brave Search API key (free tier available).

env_keys.name: BRAVE_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Brave Search API key

recipes.warning: npm fetch on first run can take 5–15 s.

recipes.description: Read and write a local SQLite database. The model gets read_query, write_query, create_table, list_tables, and describe_table tools scoped to the database file you point it at.

config_options.name: db_path
config_options.description: Absolute path to the SQLite database file. The file is created if it does not exist.

recipes.warning: Python server (PyPI mcp-server-sqlite) launched via uvx; requires uv installed. First run downloads the package (5–15 s).

recipes.description: Read-only access to a PostgreSQL database. The model gets query and schema-introspection tools against the connection string you supply.

env_keys.name: POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING
env_keys.display: Postgres connection string

recipes.warning: npm fetch on first run can take 5–15 s.

recipes.description: Read channels, post messages, search, and look up users in your Slack workspace via Slack’s official remote MCP server. Sign in with Slack (OAuth + PKCE — no token to paste). Advanced: supply bot + app-level tokens to use the legacy stdio server instead.
recipes.warning: OAuth sign-in requires the Kameas Slack app to be registered (client_id placeholder — set KAMEAS_SLACK_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID at build time or register the app and bake the client_id). Advanced: use the token-based stdio server below (id: slack-tokens).

recipes.description: Read channels, post messages, and look up users in a Slack workspace using a bot token and app-level token. Advanced fallback — prefer the ‘Slack’ recipe (remote MCP, OAuth sign-in) for token-free setup.

env_keys.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Slack bot token (xoxb-)

env_keys.name: SLACK_APP_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Slack app-level token (xapp-)

recipes.warning: npm fetch on first run can take 5–15 s. Prefer the ‘Slack’ recipe (remote MCP, OAuth sign-in) instead.

recipes.description: Read, search, send, draft, and label Gmail messages through the Gmail API. Requires a Google Cloud OAuth 2.0 credentials file (~/.gmail-mcp/gcp-oauth.keys.json). The install dialog includes a step-by-step guided setup — no command-line work needed.
recipes.warning: One-time Google Cloud setup required. The install dialog will guide you through creating an OAuth 2.0 client in the Google Cloud Console and placing the credentials file in ~/.gmail-mcp/. After install the server opens a browser sign-in once to authorize access (credentials cached at ~/.gmail-mcp/credentials.json). First npm fetch can take 10–20 s.

recipes.description: Read, search, send, and organize Outlook mail — plus calendar and contacts — via the Microsoft Graph API. Signs in with a device code in your browser on first use; personal accounts need no credentials.

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure app client ID (optional — for work/school accounts)

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure tenant ID (optional — defaults to 'common'; 'consumers' for personal)

recipes.warning: First use triggers a device-code sign-in: the server prints a URL + code for you to authorize in your browser. Personal accounts work out of the box; work/school accounts may require a custom Azure app (set the optional client/tenant IDs above). First npm fetch can take 10–20 s.

recipes.description: Time-zone aware utilities: get the current time in a given IANA timezone, convert times between zones. No credentials required.
recipes.warning: Python server (PyPI mcp-server-time) launched via uvx; requires uv installed. First run downloads the package (5–15 s).

recipes.description: Read git history, diff, blame, and branch metadata for a single repository checkout. The recipe is read-only by default and is scoped to the repo path you select.

config_options.name: repo_path
config_options.description: Absolute path to the git working tree the model is allowed to inspect.

recipes.warning: Python server (PyPI mcp-server-git) launched via uvx; requires uv installed. First run downloads the package (5–15 s).

recipes.description: Read and write Notion pages, databases, blocks, and comments. Sign in with Notion — no token to paste.
recipes.warning: Notion MCP is in beta — tool surface may change across Notion releases.

recipes.description: Connect to thousands of apps via Zapier’s official remote MCP server. Run Zaps, browse available actions, and trigger automations from the model. Sign in with Zapier (OAuth — no token to paste). Supports a fallback connection token if OAuth is unavailable.

env_keys.name: ZAPIER_MCP_CONNECTION_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Zapier MCP connection token (optional — fallback if OAuth unavailable)

recipes.description: Access 250+ tools across GitHub, Slack, Linear, Notion, and more via Composio's remote MCP server. Each user gets a unique MCP server URL from the Composio dashboard. Requires a Composio API key and your personal MCP server ID.

env_keys.name: COMPOSIO_SERVER_ID
env_keys.display: Composio MCP server ID (from Composio dashboard — the ID portion of your MCP URL)

env_keys.name: COMPOSIO_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Composio API key (from app.composio.dev/developers)

recipes.description: Trigger and inspect n8n workflows via the n8n MCP server. Works with self-hosted and n8n Cloud instances. Supply your instance hostname (e.g. myorg.app.n8n.cloud) and the MCP access token generated in your n8n instance settings.

env_keys.name: N8N_INSTANCE_HOST
env_keys.display: n8n instance hostname (e.g. myorg.app.n8n.cloud for n8n Cloud, or your self-hosted domain)

env_keys.name: N8N_MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN
env_keys.display: n8n MCP access token (from Instance Settings > MCP > Access Token tab)

recipes.warning: Workflows must be individually marked 'Available in MCP' in your n8n instance before they appear as tools. For n8n Cloud, your hostname is <slug>.app.n8n.cloud. For self-hosted n8n, use your instance's domain name (without https://).

recipes.description: Run recipes and trigger workflows in your Workato workspace via Workato's Enterprise MCP server. Each collection has its own MCP URL — copy it from AI Hub > Enterprise MCP in your Workato account.

env_keys.name: WORKATO_MCP_PATH
env_keys.display: Workato MCP collection path (the path portion of your MCP URL from AI Hub > Enterprise MCP, e.g. mcp/your-collection-id)

env_keys.name: WORKATO_MCP_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Workato Developer MCP token (from AI Hub > Enterprise MCP > Developer MCP Token)

recipes.warning: Workato Enterprise MCP requires an Enterprise plan. Your Workato admin must add you to a user group with MCP access. Each MCP server collection has its own URL — copy the path portion from AI Hub > Enterprise MCP (everything after app.workato.com/).

recipes.description: Browse, search, upload, download, and organize files in Microsoft OneDrive. Signs in with a device code in your browser on first use; personal accounts need no credentials.

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure app client ID (optional — for work/school accounts)

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure tenant ID (optional — set 'consumers' for personal; tenant ID for org)

recipes.warning: Personal Microsoft accounts: if your session expires after ~1 hour, set MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID=consumers. Work/school accounts: set MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID to your Azure tenant ID (or use a custom MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID if your org blocks third-party apps).

recipes.description: Read and send messages in Teams chats and channels, manage team members, list meetings, and fetch transcripts. Requires a work or school Microsoft account — personal accounts are not supported by Teams.

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure tenant ID (required for org sign-in — enter your organisation's tenant ID or 'common')

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure app client ID (optional — use a custom app if your org blocks third-party apps)

recipes.warning: Teams requires a work or school Microsoft account. Personal Microsoft accounts will fail at sign-in. If your organisation's IT policy blocks the default app, set MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID to your custom Azure AD app client ID and MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID to your tenant ID.

recipes.description: Search SharePoint sites, read and write lists and list items, manage list columns, and navigate site drives. Also exposes shared-mailbox and org-presence tools (work preset). Requires a work or school Microsoft account and your Azure tenant ID.

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure tenant ID (required — SharePoint is an org resource; enter your organisation's tenant ID)

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure app client ID (optional — use a custom app if your org blocks third-party apps)

recipes.warning: SharePoint requires a work or school Microsoft account and your Azure tenant ID (set MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID). The 'work' preset also exposes shared-mailbox and user-management tools alongside SharePoint. If your organisation's IT policy blocks the default app, set MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID to your custom Azure AD app client ID.

recipes.description: Read and edit Excel workbooks stored in OneDrive via the Microsoft Graph workbook API — list worksheets, read and write ranges, and manage workbook data. Signs in with a device code in your browser on first use.

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID

env_keys.name: MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID
env_keys.display: Azure tenant ID (optional — defaults to 'common'; 'consumers' for personal)

recipes.warning: First use triggers a device-code sign-in: the server prints a URL + code for you to authorize in your browser. Works on Excel files stored in OneDrive. In-workbench (served) use requires an image with the vendored Node runtime lane (US4). Word and PowerPoint have no Microsoft Graph content-editing API, so no equivalent presets exist — use the OneDrive connector for those files. First npm fetch can take 10–20 s.

recipes.description: Query databases, manage tables, run migrations, and access Supabase projects. Sign in with Supabase (OAuth) — no token to paste. For CI/headless environments, supply a personal access token as a fallback.

env_keys.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Supabase personal access token (optional — CI fallback only)

recipes.warning: Supabase MCP is intended for development and testing — do not connect to production databases. Scopes are currently all-or-nothing (write access to all available features).

recipes.description: Search repositories, read files, manage merge requests and issues, and access GitLab projects. Sign in with GitLab (OAuth) — no token to paste — or supply a personal access token as a fallback.

env_keys.name: GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
env_keys.display: GitLab personal access token (optional — fallback if you don't sign in)

recipes.warning: This recipe connects to gitlab.com only. Self-managed GitLab instances have a different MCP URL — use the custom MCP add flow for those.

recipes.description: Geocode addresses, get directions, search for places, and calculate distances via the Google Maps APIs. Requires a Google Maps API key with the relevant APIs enabled.

env_keys.name: GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Google Maps API key

recipes.warning: npm fetch on first run can take 5–15 s. Enable the Geocoding API, Directions API, Places API, and Distance Matrix API in your Google Cloud project.

recipes.description: Query Okta users, groups, apps, logs, and policies via the Okta Admin Management API. Read-only by default (okta.users.read, okta.groups.read, okta.apps.read, okta.logs.read). Sign in with device authorization (browser) or Private Key JWT. Requires your Okta org URL and an Okta app integration.

env_keys.name: OKTA_ORG_URL
env_keys.display: Okta org URL (e.g. https://yourcompany.okta.com)

env_keys.name: OKTA_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Okta app integration Client ID

env_keys.name: OKTA_SCOPES
env_keys.display: Space-separated Okta scopes (default: okta.users.read okta.groups.read okta.apps.read okta.logs.read — read-only)

env_keys.name: OKTA_PRIVATE_KEY
env_keys.display: Okta private key PEM string (optional — for Private Key JWT / server-to-server auth)

env_keys.name: OKTA_KEY_ID
env_keys.display: Okta key ID / KID (optional — required with OKTA_PRIVATE_KEY)

recipes.warning: Security read-only by default. The OKTA_SCOPES env var controls which tools are loaded — omitting manage scopes prevents write operations. recipes.description: Read accounting transactions, contacts, and settings from Xero — read-only, no transactions initiated. Uses Xero's official npm MCP package. Requires a Kameas Xero OAuth app (register at developer.xero.com).

env_keys.name: XERO_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Xero OAuth client ID (from your Kameas app at developer.xero.com)

env_keys.name: XERO_CLIENT_SECRET
env_keys.display: Xero OAuth client secret (from your Kameas app at developer.xero.com)

env_keys.name: XERO_SCOPES
env_keys.display: Xero OAuth scopes (optional — defaults to read-only accounting scopes)

recipes.warning: Owner must register a Kameas Xero OAuth app at developer.xero.com before use. Set XERO_CLIENT_ID and XERO_CLIENT_SECRET. Default scopes: accounting.transactions.read accounting.contacts.read accounting.settings.read. Verify DCR availability at identity.xero.com at build — if DCR is present, this recipe can be upgraded to zero-app. First npm fetch can take 5–15 s.

recipes.description: Read accounting data from QuickBooks Online — read-only, no transactions initiated. Requires your own Intuit OAuth app (register at developer.intuit.com); Kameas does not register or host it for you.

env_keys.name: QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Intuit/QuickBooks OAuth client ID (bring your own — from developer.intuit.com)

env_keys.name: QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_SECRET
env_keys.display: Intuit/QuickBooks OAuth client secret (from developer.intuit.com)

recipes.warning: Owner must register their own Intuit app at developer.intuit.com before use — Kameas does not register or host it. Community MCP package quickbooks-mcp (pinned 0.5.2); QuickBooks Online exposes no read-only accounting scope, so restrict tool use to reads.

recipes.description: Read Brex card expenses, transactions, and account data — read-only, no transactions initiated. Uses a Brex API token (no Kameas app registration needed — generate a token at developer.brex.com).

env_keys.name: BREX_API_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Brex API token (read-only — from developer.brex.com or the Brex dashboard)

recipes.warning: Prefer the API-token path (BREX_API_TOKEN) over OAuth to avoid Kameas app registration. Verify best npm MCP package for Brex at build — 'brex-mcp-server' is a placeholder. If OAuth2 path is required, register a Kameas Brex app at accounts.brex.com; use read-only scopes only: expenses.readonly transactions.readonly accounts.readonly. Read-only — no transfers or payment-initiation tools.

recipes.description: Read employee profiles, org groups, and HR structure from Rippling. Read-only — no payroll-run or admin writes. Requires your own Rippling OAuth app (register at developer.rippling.com); Kameas does not register or host it for you.

env_keys.name: RIPPLING_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Rippling OAuth client ID (bring your own — from developer.rippling.com)

env_keys.name: RIPPLING_CLIENT_SECRET
env_keys.display: Rippling OAuth client secret (from developer.rippling.com)

recipes.warning: Owner must register their own Rippling OAuth2 app at developer.rippling.com before use — Kameas does not register or host it. Note: Rippling supports PKCE S256 but no DCR — an operator-registered app is required. Scopes are defined at app-registration time; request minimal read-only scopes (employees, groups, org). Verify best npm MCP package for Rippling at build — 'rippling-mcp-server' is a placeholder. Auth endpoints: authorize=https://app.rippling.com/oauth token=https://api.rippling.com/o/token/. No payroll-run tools.

recipes.description: Enterprise — NetSuite uses per-account Token-Based Authentication (TBA) or OAuth2, both requiring per-tenant setup. No community MCP package confirmed at research time. For quick read-only access to NetSuite data, connect via Zapier or Workato in the Automation section.

env_keys.name: NETSUITE_ACCOUNT_ID
env_keys.display: NetSuite account ID (e.g. 1234567 — from your NetSuite account URL)

env_keys.name: NETSUITE_CONSUMER_KEY
env_keys.display: NetSuite TBA consumer key

env_keys.name: NETSUITE_CONSUMER_SECRET
env_keys.display: NetSuite TBA consumer secret

env_keys.name: NETSUITE_TOKEN_ID
env_keys.display: NetSuite TBA token ID

env_keys.name: NETSUITE_TOKEN_SECRET
env_keys.display: NetSuite TBA token secret

config_options.name: netsuite_account_id
config_options.description: Your NetSuite account ID — the numeric portion of your NetSuite URL (e.g. 1234567 from 1234567.app.netsuite.com)

recipes.warning: Enterprise — requires NetSuite TBA setup by a NetSuite administrator. Community MCP package netsuite-mcp-server (pinned 1.0.2).

recipes.description: Enterprise — Workday uses tenant-specific URLs and ISU (Integration System User) or OAuth2 client credentials, both requiring per-tenant setup by a Workday administrator. No confirmed community MCP package as of July 2026. For quick access to Workday HR data, connect via Zapier or Workato in the Automation section.

env_keys.name: WORKDAY_ISU_USERNAME
env_keys.display: Workday ISU username (Integration System User — from your Workday tenant)

env_keys.name: WORKDAY_ISU_PASSWORD
env_keys.display: Workday ISU password (from your Workday tenant)

config_options.name: workday_tenant_url
config_options.description: Your Workday tenant URL — e.g. https://acmecorp.workday.com (from your Workday admin)

recipes.warning: Enterprise — requires Workday ISU setup by a Workday administrator. No confirmed community MCP package at research time; 'workday-mcp' is a placeholder — verify at developer.workday.com at build. For quick access to Workday HR data, connect via Zapier or Workato in the Automation section instead.

recipes.description: Query Grafana Cloud dashboards, datasources, incidents, and alerts. Sign in with your Grafana Cloud account — no token to paste.
recipes.warning: Grafana Cloud only — self-hosted Grafana OSS does not expose a remote MCP server.

recipes.description: Query Datadog metrics, monitors, dashboards, logs, incidents, and infrastructure. Sign in with your Datadog account — no token to paste. Supports US1 site by default; configure for EU or other regions.

env_keys.name: DD_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Datadog API key (optional — fallback for non-OAuth auth)

env_keys.name: DD_APPLICATION_KEY
env_keys.display: Datadog Application key (optional — required with DD_API_KEY fallback)

config_options.name: datadog_site
config_options.description: Override for non-US1 Datadog sites. EU: https://mcp.datadoghq.eu/v1/mcp; US3: https://mcp.us3.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp; US5: https://mcp.us5.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp.

recipes.warning: GovCloud sites (ddog-gov.com) not supported. Rate limit: 50 req/10 s, 50 k calls/month.

recipes.description: Query New Relic observability data including APM, infrastructure, logs, and alerts. Sign in with your New Relic account — no token to paste.

Query Dynatrace observability data — problems, monitored entities, and DQL queries over Grail — via the official Dynatrace remote MCP endpoint on your environment. Authenticates with a Dynatrace platform token.

env_keys.name: DYNATRACE_ENVIRONMENT_NAME
env_keys.display: Dynatrace environment name (the <env> in <env>.apps.dynatrace.com)

env_keys.name: DYNATRACE_PLATFORM_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Dynatrace platform token (Account Management → Platform tokens)

recipes.warning: The endpoint URL is environment-specific (<env>.apps.dynatrace.com). Direct remote MCP access does not support public OAuth clients — Dynatrace recommends platform tokens; tokens minted from OAuth clients are short-lived and need manual refresh.

recipes.description: Search and analyze Splunk platform data via the official MCP Server for Splunk (streamable HTTP), installed as a Splunkbase app on your Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud Platform deployment.

env_keys.name: SPLUNK_MCP_ENDPOINT
env_keys.display: Splunk MCP endpoint host + path, without https:// (shown in the Splunk MCP Server app)

env_keys.name: SPLUNK_MCP_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Encrypted MCP token (generated in the Splunk MCP Server app)

recipes.warning: Requires the Splunk MCP Server app (Splunkbase 7931) installed on your Splunk Enterprise (9.3+) or Splunk Cloud Platform deployment. Copy the endpoint and an encrypted MCP token from the app — encrypted tokens work only for MCP, not for direct Splunk API calls.

recipes.description: Query CircleCI pipelines, workflows, jobs, and build artifacts. Sign in with your CircleCI account — no token to paste.
Manage Netlify sites, deploys, environment variables, and domain configuration. Sign in with your Netlify account — no token to paste.
recipes.warning: Netlify MCP server is hosted at netlify-mcp.netlify.app. Stdio alternative available via 'npx -y @netlify/mcp' for offline use.

recipes.description: Manage Vercel projects, deployments, domains, and environment variables. Sign in with your Vercel account — no token to paste.

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_VERCEL_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Your Vercel OAuth client ID (bring your own — Kameas does not provide one)

recipes.warning: Vercel MCP only supports AI clients reviewed and approved by Vercel — DCR registrations from unknown clients may be blocked. Requires your own Vercel OAuth integration — register one at vercel.com and add its client ID in the connector's setup below. Kameas does not register or host it for you.

recipes.description: Search and manage Bitbucket Cloud repositories, pull requests, and pipelines via the Atlassian MCP server. Sign in with your Atlassian account.

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_ATLASSIAN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Your Atlassian OAuth client ID (bring your own — Kameas does not provide one)

recipes.warning: Requires Bitbucket Cloud account. Uses the same Atlassian OAuth app as the Jira/Confluence connector — bring your own app (register at developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps); Kameas does not register or host it for you. Add its client ID in the connector's setup below.

recipes.description: Query PagerDuty incidents, services, schedules, on-call assignments, and alerts. Requires a PagerDuty User API Token. Read-only by default.

env_keys.name: PAGERDUTY_USER_API_KEY
env_keys.display: PagerDuty User API Token

recipes.warning: uvx downloads pagerduty-mcp package on first run (5–15 s). EU accounts: set PAGERDUTY_API_HOST=https://api.eu.pagerduty.com. Write tools are disabled by default (omit --enable-write-tools to stay read-only).

recipes.description: Run Snyk security scans: SAST, SCA (open-source), IaC, and container vulnerability analysis. Requires a Snyk API token.

env_keys.name: SNYK_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Snyk API token (from Snyk account settings → API token)

recipes.warning: npm downloads snyk package on first run (5–15 s). Snyk CLI requires Node.js to be available. SNYK_TOKEN can also be set as SNYK_AUTH_TOKEN for older CLI versions.

recipes.description: Analyse code quality and security with SonarQube Server or SonarCloud via the official SonarSource MCP server. Requires Docker and a SonarQube user token.

env_keys.name: SONARQUBE_TOKEN
env_keys.display: SonarQube / SonarCloud user token

config_options.name: sonar_url
config_options.description: SonarCloud: https://sonarcloud.io. Self-hosted SonarQube Server: your instance URL (e.g. https://sonar.mycompany.com).

config_options.name: sonar_org
config_options.description: Required for SonarCloud. Your organisation key from SonarCloud Settings. Omit for self-hosted SonarQube Server.

recipes.warning: Requires Docker installed locally. First run pulls sonarsource/sonarqube-mcp image (may take 1–2 min). Use a User token — project/global/scoped tokens will not work with the MCP server.

recipes.description: Query Jenkins builds, pipelines, jobs, nodes, and artifacts. Requires a running Jenkins instance with the MCP Server Plugin installed.

env_keys.name: JENKINS_INSTANCE_HOST
env_keys.display: Jenkins instance hostname (e.g. jenkins.mycompany.com or 192.168.1.10:8080)

env_keys.name: JENKINS_BASIC_AUTH
env_keys.display: Jenkins Basic auth credentials (base64 of user:api-token — see Jenkins user profile → API Token)

recipes.warning: Requires Jenkins MCP Server Plugin installed. Plugin exposes MCP at https://<your-jenkins>/mcp-server/mcp. JENKINS_BASIC_AUTH must be base64(username:api-token). Jenkins must be network-accessible from your machine.

recipes.description: List, create, and update Google Calendar events via a stdio MCP server. Supports calendar.events (read + write) and calendar.readonly scopes. Requires one-time sign-in — reuses same Google Cloud OAuth client (gcp-oauth.keys.json) as Gmail if already set up.

env_keys.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS
env_keys.display: Path to saved Google OAuth credentials file (auto-created on first browser sign-in)

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Kameas Google OAuth client ID (provided — no action needed when using built-in install flow)

recipes.warning: One-time setup required: create or reuse a Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app type), save gcp-oauth.keys.json and set GOOGLE_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS path, then complete browser sign-in when prompted. Tokens expire weekly in Google test-mode; completing Google app verification removes this limit. If you already set up Gmail, reuse the same gcp-oauth.keys.json — just re-authorize to include Calendar scopes. First npm fetch can take 10–20 s.

recipes.description: Search, read, and create files in Google Drive. Uses drive.file scope (access limited to files created by this app) — upgrade to full drive.readonly access requires Google security review (CASA). Requires one-time Google sign-in (reuses same Google Cloud OAuth client as Gmail and Calendar).

env_keys.name: GDRIVE_OAUTH_PATH
env_keys.display: Path to Google OAuth keys file (gcp-oauth.keys.json)

env_keys.name: GDRIVE_CREDENTIALS_PATH
env_keys.display: Path to saved Drive credentials file (auto-created on first sign-in)

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Kameas Google OAuth client ID (provided — no action needed when using built-in install flow)

recipes.warning: One-time Google OAuth setup required: create or reuse a Google Cloud OAuth client (Desktop app type), save gcp-oauth.keys.json and set GDRIVE_OAUTH_PATH to its location. On first run the server opens a browser sign-in to authorize access; credentials are cached at GDRIVE_CREDENTIALS_PATH. Current scope is drive.file (app-created files only); upgrade to drive.readonly requires Google OAuth app verification + annual CASA third-party security assessment. If you already set up Gmail or Calendar, reuse the same gcp-oauth.keys.json. First npm fetch can take 10–20 s.

recipes.description: Read, create, and edit Google Docs documents via Google's official Workspace remote MCP server. Sign in with Google (OAuth).
recipes.warning: Developer preview (Google Workspace Developer Preview Program). Google does not support dynamic client registration: sign-in needs a Google Cloud OAuth client (client_id placeholder — register the Kameas Google OAuth app or supply your own project's client) with the Google Docs API and the Docs MCP service enabled in that project.

recipes.description: Read, create, and edit Google Sheets spreadsheets via Google's official Workspace remote MCP server. Sign in with Google (OAuth).
recipes.warning: Developer preview (Google Workspace Developer Preview Program). Google does not support dynamic client registration: sign-in needs a Google Cloud OAuth client (client_id placeholder — register the Kameas Google OAuth app or supply your own project's client) with the Google Sheets API and the Sheets MCP service enabled in that project.

recipes.description: Manage tasks, docs, and chat in ClickUp — search, create, update tasks and projects. Sign in with ClickUp — no token to paste.
Access boards, items, workflows, and automations in Monday.com. Sign in with Monday — no token to paste — or supply a personal API token.

env_keys.name: MONDAY_API_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Monday.com personal API token (optional — fallback if you don't sign in)

recipes.description: Search stories, create and update epics, iterations, and sprints in Shortcut. Sign in with Shortcut — no token to paste.
Read and update Smartsheet sheets, rows, columns, workspaces, and dashboards. Sign in with your Smartsheet account.

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_SMARTSHEET_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Your Smartsheet OAuth client ID (bring your own — Kameas does not provide one)

recipes.warning: Requires your own Smartsheet OAuth app, registered at developers.smartsheet.com; Kameas does not register or host it for you. Add its client ID in the connector's setup below to activate sign-in.

recipes.description: Search tasks, projects, and folders in Wrike; create and update work items. Sign in with your Wrike account.

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_WRIKE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Your Wrike OAuth client ID (bring your own — Kameas does not provide one)

env_keys.name: WRIKE_PERMANENT_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Wrike Permanent Access Token (optional — fallback for headless/automation use)

config_options.name: datacenter
config_options.description: EU customers: select 'eu' to use app-eu.wrike.com endpoints.

recipes.warning: Requires your own Wrike OAuth app, registered at wrike.com/frontend/apps/index.html#/api; Kameas does not register or host it for you. Add its client ID in the connector's setup below to activate sign-in. EU customers: set datacenter=eu to use app-eu.wrike.com endpoints.

recipes.description: Manage Trello boards, lists, and cards — search, create, update via the Trello REST API. Requires a Trello API key and token.

env_keys.name: TRELLO_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Trello API key (from trello.com/power-ups/admin)

env_keys.name: TRELLO_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Trello OAuth token — generate at: https://trello.com/1/authorize?key=YOUR_KEY&scope=read,write&expiration=never&response_type=token

recipes.warning: Uses community package @delorenj/mcp-server-trello (verify at build — check license and maintenance). Trello uses API key + OAuth 1.0 token (not OAuth 2.0). Generate your token at: https://trello.com/1/authorize?key=YOUR_API_KEY&scope=read,write&expiration=never&response_type=token. npm fetch on first run can take 5–15 s.

recipes.description: Read and write Coda docs, pages, tables, and rows via the Coda API. Requires a Coda API token.

env_keys.name: CODA_API_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Coda API token (from coda.io/account → API Settings)

recipes.warning: Coda is transitioning to Superhuman Docs (coda.io now redirects to docs.superhuman.com). This recipe targets the current Coda API; verify compatibility if you have recently migrated. Uses community package mcp-server-coda — verify at build (check license and maintenance). npm fetch on first run can take 5–15 s.

recipes.description: Query Mixpanel analytics: events, funnels, retention, segmentation, insights, cohorts, and business context via Mixpanel's official remote MCP server. Sign in with Mixpanel (OAuth DCR — no token paste, no app registration required). US region default; EU/IN URL configurable.

config_options.name: mixpanel_server_url
config_options.display: Mixpanel MCP server URL (override for EU/IN region)
config_options.description: US default: https://mcp.mixpanel.com/mcp. EU/IN variants: verify server URLs at build — not live-confirmed.

recipes.warning: DCR zero-app: sign-in is token-free. Read-only analytics access — no data ingestion or project-admin tools. EU/IN server URLs not live-confirmed; verify at build.

recipes.description: Query Amplitude analytics: events, funnels, user behavior, and product insights via Amplitude's official remote MCP server. Sign in with Amplitude (OAuth DCR — no token paste, no app registration required). US region default; EU region configurable.

config_options.name: amplitude_server_url
config_options.display: Amplitude MCP server URL (override for EU region)
config_options.description: US default: https://mcp.amplitude.com/mcp. EU: https://mcp.eu.amplitude.com/mcp (live-verified). Append ?discovery=progressive to reduce token overhead (optional).

recipes.warning: DCR zero-app: sign-in is token-free. EU region: use https://mcp.eu.amplitude.com/mcp. Append ?discovery=progressive to the URL to reduce token overhead.

recipes.description: Access Klaviyo marketing automation: campaigns, flows, lists, profiles, metrics, segments, and templates via Klaviyo's official remote MCP server. Sign in with Klaviyo (OAuth DCR — no token paste, no app registration required). Scopes derived from private key permissions.
recipes.warning: DCR zero-app: sign-in is token-free. Scopes are assigned by Klaviyo based on your private key permissions (Accounts, Campaigns, Catalogs, Events, Flows, Images, Lists, Metrics, Profiles, Segments, Subscriptions, Tags, Templates, Translations). No scopes declared in recipe — server assigns based on key.

recipes.description: Query dbt Cloud: explore models, lineage, docs, jobs, environments, and semantic layer via dbt Cloud's remote MCP server. OAuth DCR (Enterprise+) or personal access token. Per-workspace URL supported. Consumption-only — no dbt run or build triggers.

env_keys.name: DBT_ACCESS_TOKEN
env_keys.display: dbt Cloud personal access token (fallback for non-Enterprise plans)

env_keys.name: DBT_PROD_ENV_ID
env_keys.display: dbt Cloud production environment ID (optional — for semantic layer queries)

config_options.name: dbt_host
config_options.display: dbt Cloud instance hostname (e.g. cloud.getdbt.com or your custom domain)
config_options.description: Per-workspace hostname. Default: cloud.getdbt.com. Custom domains: replace with your dbt Cloud subdomain.

recipes.warning: DCR supported on Enterprise+ plans; token-based works on all plans (set DBT_ACCESS_TOKEN). MCP URL is per-account — override dbt_host config_option for custom domains. Consumption-only: read/query only, no dbt run/build. DCR registration_endpoint auth-gated at discovery time; verify at build.

recipes.description: Query Tableau Cloud: browse datasources, workbooks, views, Pulse insights, and site content via Tableau's official remote MCP server. Sign in with Tableau (OAuth PKCE — requires your own Connected App registration). Read-only access.

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_TABLEAU_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Your Tableau OAuth client ID (bring your own — from a Connected App you register in Tableau Cloud Admin; Kameas does not provide one)

recipes.warning: Owner action required: register your own Connected App in Tableau Cloud Admin (Connected Apps > Create Connected App); Kameas does not register or host it for you. Redirect URI: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback (the harness's local loopback listener — NOT app.kameas.ai). Add the client ID in the connector's setup below once registered. Auth server: sso.online.tableau.com (no DCR — PKCE only). Read-only scopes; no write/admin tools.

recipes.description: Inspect Fivetran connectors, schemas, sync history, and metadata via the official Fivetran MCP server. Read-only by default (FIVETRAN_ALLOW_WRITES not set). API key + secret authentication.

env_keys.name: FIVETRAN_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Fivetran API key (from Fivetran Dashboard > API Config)

env_keys.name: FIVETRAN_API_SECRET
env_keys.display: Fivetran API secret (from Fivetran Dashboard > API Config)

recipes.warning: Installs directly from the official Fivetran GitHub repo, pinned to commit d5bf139. Requires uv installed.

recipes.description: Query Amazon Redshift data warehouse via the official AWS Labs MCP server. Read-only access using AWS IAM credentials (profile or environment credentials). Supports cluster and Serverless endpoints.

env_keys.name: AWS_PROFILE
env_keys.display: AWS profile name (from ~/.aws/credentials; use 'default' if unsure)

env_keys.name: AWS_REGION
env_keys.display: AWS region (e.g. us-east-1)

config_options.name: cluster_identifier
config_options.display: Redshift cluster identifier (for provisioned cluster; omit for Serverless)
config_options.description: Provisioned cluster identifier. Leave empty for Redshift Serverless (uses workgroup instead).

recipes.warning: Amazon Redshift via the official AWS Labs package awslabs.redshift-mcp-server (pinned 0.0.30), launched with uvx; requires uv installed. AWS IAM credentials must be configured (aws configure or environment variables).

recipes.description: Query Snowflake data warehouse via community MCP server. Read-only access (no --allow_write flag). Connection credentials passed as CLI flags. Supports account, user, password, warehouse, database, schema, and role.

env_keys.name: SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT
env_keys.display: Snowflake account identifier (e.g. myorg-myaccount or myaccount.us-east-1)

env_keys.name: SNOWFLAKE_USER
env_keys.display: Snowflake username

env_keys.name: SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD
env_keys.display: Snowflake password

env_keys.name: SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE
env_keys.display: Snowflake virtual warehouse name

env_keys.name: SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE
env_keys.display: Snowflake database name

env_keys.name: SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA
env_keys.display: Snowflake schema name (e.g. PUBLIC)

env_keys.name: SNOWFLAKE_ROLE
env_keys.display: Snowflake role (e.g. SYSADMIN, ANALYST)

recipes.warning: Community package (PyPI mcp_server_snowflake). Password is read from the SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD environment variable, not the command line. Read-only unless the server is started with a write flag.

recipes.description: Query Google BigQuery data warehouse via Google's genai-toolbox MCP server. Read-only access using Application Default Credentials (ADC) or service account key file. No official Google remote MCP server exists yet.

env_keys.name: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
env_keys.display: Path to Google service account key JSON file (leave empty to use Application Default Credentials)

config_options.name: project_id
config_options.description: Google Cloud project ID containing the BigQuery datasets to query.

recipes.warning: Google-maintained genai-toolbox (npm @toolbox-sdk/server --prebuilt=bigquery). Verify exact --prebuilt=bigquery flag syntax and project_id config arg at build (toolbox docs at mcp-toolbox.dev). ADC or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS for auth. First npm fetch can take 5–15 s.

recipes.description: Query Metabase: browse questions, dashboards, databases, and run queries via community MCP server. Works with self-hosted and Metabase Cloud instances. API key authentication recommended (Metabase v0.47+).

env_keys.name: METABASE_URL
env_keys.display: Metabase instance URL (e.g. https://your-metabase.example.com or https://your-company.metabaseapp.com)

env_keys.name: METABASE_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Metabase API key (recommended; requires Metabase v0.47+)

env_keys.name: METABASE_USER_EMAIL
env_keys.display: Metabase user email (fallback if API key not used)

env_keys.name: METABASE_PASSWORD
env_keys.display: Metabase password (fallback if API key not used)

recipes.warning: Community package (PyPI metabase-mcp v1.0.0). API key auth recommended (Metabase v0.47+); email/password fallback for older versions. METABASE_URL must point to your specific Metabase instance. Requires uv installed.

recipes.description: Query Looker: browse explores, run LookML queries, access dashboards and looks via community MCP server. Uses Looker API3 key (client_id + client_secret). Works with self-hosted Looker and Looker Cloud.

env_keys.name: LOOKER_BASE_URL
env_keys.display: Looker instance base URL (e.g. https://your-company.looker.com)

env_keys.name: LOOKER_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Looker API3 client ID (from Admin > Users > API3 Keys)

env_keys.name: LOOKER_CLIENT_SECRET
env_keys.display: Looker API3 client secret (from Admin > Users > API3 Keys)

recipes.warning: Community package (PyPI looker-mcp v0.1.0 — not Google-official). Env var prefix is LOOKER_* (not LOOKERSDK_*). A Google-official Looker MCP may supersede this. Requires uv installed. First run downloads package (5–15 s).

recipes.description: Query GA4 analytics: dimensions, metrics, reports, and real-time data via community MCP server. Uses Google service account credentials (Application Default Credentials or JSON key file). No official Google remote MCP server for GA4.

env_keys.name: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
env_keys.display: Path to Google service account key JSON file (or use Application Default Credentials via gcloud auth)

env_keys.name: GA4_PROPERTY_ID
env_keys.display: GA4 property ID (numeric, e.g. 123456789 — from GA4 Admin > Property Settings)

recipes.warning: Community package (PyPI google-analytics-mcp v2.8.1 — not Google-official). Uses GA4 Data API with service account auth. Enable Google Analytics Data API in Google Cloud Console. No official Google MCP for GA4 as of 2026-07-21 — future official server may supersede. Requires uv installed.

recipes.description: Access Mailchimp: campaigns, lists, audiences, templates, and analytics via community MCP server. API key authentication — datacenter derived from the API key suffix (e.g. -us6).

env_keys.name: MAILCHIMP_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Mailchimp API key (from Mailchimp Account > Extras > API keys; datacenter derived from key suffix)

recipes.warning: Community package (PyPI mcp-mailchimp v0.3.0 — not Mailchimp-official). Only MAILCHIMP_API_KEY is needed; datacenter/server prefix is derived from the key suffix (e.g. key ending in -us6 → us6 datacenter). No separate server prefix env var needed. Requires uv installed.

recipes.description: Access Braze: campaigns, segments, canvases, content blocks, subscription groups, and analytics via the Braze-maintained MCP server. Read-only access using API key + cluster endpoint. BRAZE_ALLOW_WRITES not set (read-only enforcement).

env_keys.name: BRAZE_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Braze REST API key (create with least-privilege read-only permissions in Braze > Settings > API Keys)

env_keys.name: BRAZE_BASE_URL
env_keys.display: Braze cluster REST endpoint (e.g. https://rest.iad-01.braze.com — see Braze dashboard URL for cluster)

recipes.warning: Braze-affiliated package (PyPI braze-mcp-server v1.2.0). Read-only: BRAZE_ALLOW_WRITES not set. Use a least-privilege API key with only the read permissions your use case requires. BRAZE_BASE_URL is cluster-specific (e.g. rest.iad-01.braze.com, rest.eu-01.braze.com) — check your Braze dashboard URL. Requires uv installed.

recipes.description: Access Marketo: leads, programs, campaigns, forms, lists, and assets via community MCP server. Uses Marketo REST API with client credentials OAuth (client_id + client_secret + Munchkin ID). Read-only scopes. STRETCH: package unconfirmed on npm registry at planning time — verify at build.

env_keys.name: MARKETO_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Marketo API client ID (from Marketo Admin > LaunchPoint > View Details)

env_keys.name: MARKETO_CLIENT_SECRET
env_keys.display: Marketo API client secret (from Marketo Admin > LaunchPoint > View Details)

env_keys.name: MARKETO_MUNCHKIN_ID
env_keys.display: Marketo Munchkin ID (from Marketo Admin > Integration > Munchkin, e.g. 000-AAA-000)

recipes.warning: Owner must register a Marketo API client. Community MCP package marketo-mcp-server (pinned 1.4.0). First run downloads the package.

recipes.description: Query Databricks SQL warehouses and Unity Catalog via community MCP server. Uses Databricks personal access token (PAT) + workspace host. STRETCH: databricks-mcp package is a library component — verify runnable entry point and exact uvx invocation at build.

env_keys.name: DATABRICKS_HOST
env_keys.display: Databricks workspace URL (e.g. https://adb-1234567890.12.azuredatabricks.net)

env_keys.name: DATABRICKS_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Databricks personal access token (from User Settings > Developer > Access tokens)

recipes.warning: STRETCH: databricks-mcp v0.9.0 (Databricks-affiliated, PyPI) may be a library component rather than a directly runnable MCP server — verify uvx entry point and exact CLI invocation at build. If not uvx-runnable, use Databricks SQL Connector via generic SQL tool or defer. Read/query only — no cluster management or admin writes.

recipes.description: Search Elasticsearch indices and run Agent Builder tools via the Elastic Agent Builder MCP endpoint on your deployment's Kibana (Elastic Stack 9.2+ or Serverless). Authenticates with a Kibana API key.

env_keys.name: KIBANA_HOST
env_keys.display: Kibana host, without https:// (e.g. my-deployment.kb.us-east-1.aws.elastic.cloud)

env_keys.name: ELASTIC_API_KEY
env_keys.display: Kibana API key with the Agent Builder privilege

recipes.warning: Requires Elastic Stack 9.2+ (or an Elasticsearch Serverless project) with Agent Builder enabled; the API key needs the feature_agentBuilder.read Kibana privilege. For a custom Kibana space, append /s/<space> to the host value. The older stdio server (@elastic/mcp-server-elasticsearch) is deprecated.

recipes.description: Read and write Airtable bases, tables, and records. Sign in with Airtable — no token to paste.
Create, read, and edit Canva designs, folders, brand templates, and assets. Sign in with Canva — no token to paste.
Browse Figma files, components, and design tokens. Sign in with Figma — no token to paste.
Read and update Miro boards, frames, and sticky notes. Sign in with Miro — no token to paste.
recipes.warning: Miro MCP requires a Miro Enterprise plan. An org admin must enable the MCP Server integration before users can connect.

recipes.description: Browse, search, and read files and folders in Dropbox. Sign in with Dropbox — no token to paste.
Query PayPal transactions, orders, and account balance. Read/query only — no payment initiation. Sign in with PayPal — no token to paste.
recipes.warning: This recipe exposes read and query tools only. No payment-initiation or money-movement tools are enabled.

recipes.description: Query Square customers, orders, catalog items, and merchant profile. Read/query only — no payment processing. Sign in with Square — no token to paste.
recipes.warning: Square MCP is in Beta. This recipe requests read-only scopes — no payment or charge tools are enabled.

recipes.description: Search and update CRM contacts, companies, deals, and engagements in HubSpot. Sign in with HubSpot.

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_HUBSPOT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Your HubSpot OAuth client ID (bring your own — Kameas does not provide one)

recipes.warning: Requires your own HubSpot app — create one at developers.hubspot.com/apps and add its client ID in the connector's setup below. Kameas does not register or host it for you.

recipes.description: Browse, search, and read files and folders stored in Box. Sign in with Box.

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_BOX_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Your Box OAuth client ID (bring your own — from the Box Developer Console; Kameas does not provide one)

recipes.warning: Requires your own Box app — create one in the Box Developer Console (developer.box.com) and add its client ID in the connector's setup below. Kameas does not register or host it for you.

recipes.description: Search, read, and update Salesforce records (contacts, accounts, opportunities, cases). Sign in with Salesforce.

env_keys.name: KAMEAS_SALESFORCE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env_keys.display: Your Salesforce OAuth client ID (bring your own — from an External Client App you create in Salesforce Setup; Kameas does not provide one)

config_options.name: org_domain
config_options.description: Your Salesforce My Domain prefix (e.g. 'mycompany' for mycompany.my.salesforce.com).

recipes.warning: Requires your own Salesforce External Client App — create one in Salesforce Setup (see developer.salesforce.com for the connected/external app guide) and add its client ID in the connector's setup below. Kameas does not register or host it for you.

recipes.description: Search and read BigCommerce developer documentation — API references, guides, and webhooks. No authentication required.
recipes.warning: This connector provides read-only access to BigCommerce developer documentation only — not to store data.

recipes.description: Query and manage Shopify store products, orders, customers, and inventory. Requires a Shopify store Admin API access token.

env_keys.name: SHOPIFY_STORE_URL
env_keys.display: Shopify store URL (e.g. mystore.myshopify.com)

env_keys.name: SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Shopify Admin API access token

recipes.warning: Verify at build: confirm whether this Shopify MCP server exposes store data (products, orders, customers) or only developer-tooling docs. If store-data access is required, substitute a community store-data MCP package.

recipes.description: Search and update Pipedrive deals, contacts, organizations, and activities. Requires a Pipedrive API token.

env_keys.name: PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN
env_keys.display: Pipedrive API token

recipes.warning: Community MCP package pipedrive-mcp-server (pinned 2.1.0). First run downloads the package.

recipes.description: Query Stripe payments, customers, subscriptions, and invoices. Read/query only — no charge, refund, transfer, or payout tools. Requires a Stripe Restricted Key with read-only permissions.

env_keys.name: STRIPE_RESTRICTED_KEY
env_keys.display: Stripe Restricted Key (read-only — generated in Stripe Dashboard → API Keys → Restricted Keys)

recipes.warning: Read and query only — no charge, refund, transfer, payout, or other write tools are enabled. You MUST supply a Stripe Restricted Key (not a Secret Key) with read-only permissions. Never paste a full Secret Key here.
